entries.clue: Reform or Richard Tice’s getting a seat (9,5)

indicatorNotes.Reform: to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters are re-formed

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters, the S included

annotation.surface: A political jibe: the Reform party and its figure Richard Tice angling for a seat.
annotation.walkthrough: Richard Tice is a leader of Reform UK, a British political party, so 'Reform' reads as a party name and 'seat' as a parliamentary one; both are misdirection.
annotation.definitionFit: A director's chair is a folding canvas seat of the kind film directors sit in.

entries.clue: Detectives mostly bent, politician is loaded (14)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

blocks.note: bent = CRIMINAL, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: Crooked detectives and a rich politician: a picture of police and political corruption.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loaded' seems to mean rich, sitting next to 'politician'; it means biased, as in a loaded question.
annotation.definitionFit: Something loaded is weighted unfairly against someone, which is what discriminatory means.

entries.clue: Checks on son moving into stylish home (5,2)

indicatorNotes.moving into: the son moves inside the other pieces

annotation.surface: An estate agent's note: running checks on a son who is moving into a smart house.
annotation.walkthrough: The house-moving picture hides that 'stylish' and 'home' give the same two letters; 'moving into' puts the son between them.
annotation.definitionFit: To rein in is to hold back or restrain, as a rider checks a horse.

entries.clue: Jack perhaps to go out with caution during match? (5,4)

blocks.note: to court is to date, to go out with
a yellow card is the caution a referee shows in football

annotation.surface: Jack is thinking of dating someone, with a warning about what happens at the game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a man's name; it is the playing card. 'Perhaps' flags it as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: Jack, queen and king are the court cards in a pack.

entries.clue: Look after extra on picture (7)

blocks.note: to picture something is to see it in your mind

annotation.surface: An instruction on a film set: someone must look after the extras in the picture.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts OVER above SEE. The film-set surface turns 'extra' and 'picture' into an actor and a movie.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a manager who supervises staff looks after them, keeping an eye over the work.

entries.clue: Primarily, sugar-free Cola is drunk in parties (7)

indicatorNotes.drunk: a drunk is scrambled, so the letters are too

annotation.surface: A note on the soft drinks: diet cola is what gets drunk at parties.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' reads as the past tense of drink, which suits cola; here it scrambles the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A mainly British noun use: a club or church holds an evening 'social', an informal gathering, so the plural stands for parties.

entries.clue: Get out of house – mine? (3,2)

blocks.note: a pit is a mine, like a coal pit

annotation.surface: Someone ordering an intruder out: "Get out of my house – it's mine!"
annotation.walkthrough: The dash and question mark make 'mine' look possessive; it is the noun, a coal mine.
annotation.definitionFit: "Hop it!" is a British order meaning go away, get out.

entries.clue: Battle of WWII: a major shot having lost war (3,4)

indicatorNotes.shot: something shot is broken to pieces, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.having lost: the listed letters are taken out

blocks.note: W, A and R are removed, leaving WIIMAJO

annotation.surface: A military note: a major was shot in a WWII battle, and the war was lost.
annotation.walkthrough: 'WWII' reads as a date for the battle, but it is fodder: its letters, with A MAJOR, lose W, A, R before being rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: Iwo Jima was a 1945 battle between US and Japanese forces in the Pacific.

entries.clue: Resetting a line for anagram: it includes colon (5,9)

annotation.definitionNote: a description rather than a synonym

indicatorNotes.for anagram: the letters are offered as an anagram, to be rearranged

annotation.surface: A proofreader's note about resetting a line of type so an anagram fits, colon and all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Resetting' looks like the anagram indicator; it is fodder, and the indicator is the blunt 'for anagram'. The colon in the clue is also the definition's organ.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the bowel section between the small intestine and the rectum is mostly colon, so the whole includes it.

entries.clue: Fit soldiers with uniform after altering size (7)

indicatorNotes.altering: the letters of the word are changed around

blocks.note: U is uniform in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Kitting out troops: fitting soldiers with uniforms once the sizes are altered.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fit' reads as a verb about tailoring; it is the noun, a convulsion.
annotation.definitionFit: A seizure is a fit, a sudden convulsive attack.

entries.clue: Film-maker to capture clip about American (7)

indicatorNotes.about: turned about, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: to cop is to catch or capture
to lop is to clip or cut

annotation.surface: A film-maker setting out to capture a clip about America.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clip' suggests film footage beside 'Film-maker'; it is the verb, to cut. Francis Ford Coppola directed The Godfather.
annotation.definitionFit: Francis Ford Coppola (and his daughter Sofia) are film directors.

entries.clue: Clear trees for building (5)

indicatorNotes.for building: the letters are raw material to build a new word from

annotation.surface: A developer's plan: clear the trees to make way for building.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clear' looks like a verb about felling trees; it means to reset, as with a counter or a form.
annotation.definitionFit: To reset a counter or a display is to clear it back to zero.

entries.clue: Remarkable bird popping back to nest (9)

indicatorNotes.back to: the back of the word, so its last letter
indicatorNotes.popping: popping in, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: the starling is a common bird

annotation.surface: A remarkable sight: a bird popping back to its nest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Popping back to nest' reads as a bird returning home; 'back to nest' is only the final T, which pops into STARLING.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: news that makes you jump is striking enough to be worth remarking on.

entries.clue: They seduce with long hair: sweet things ditching fellow (3-6)

indicatorNotes.ditching: to ditch is to get rid of, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: a mane is a long head of hair

annotation.surface: A profile of seductresses: long flowing hair, sweet looks, and men thrown over.
annotation.walkthrough: Afters is British slang for dessert, the course that comes after the main one.
annotation.definitionFit: Man-eaters are women who seduce and discard men.

entries.clue: Perhaps ticks answer close to right one (5)

annotation.surface: A marker's note: ticks for an answer that is close to right.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ticks' reads as a teacher's marks next to 'answer' and 'right'; they are the creatures. 'Close to' is not taking a last letter here: it means about, CA.
annotation.definitionFit: Acari are mites and ticks; ticks are one example, hence 'perhaps'.

entries.clue: Provision of services is welcoming couple after conclusion of prayers (9)

indicatorNotes.welcoming: taking a guest in, so the word goes inside
indicatorNotes.after: the first piece comes before the rest

blocks.note: to couple is to tie, to join

annotation.surface: A church notice: the service welcomes a couple once the prayers are over.
annotation.walkthrough: The church setting makes 'couple' a pair at a wedding and 'services' church services; couple is the verb, to tie.
annotation.definitionFit: Amenities are useful facilities and services provided in a place.

entries.clue: Appointed journalist to follow war (5)

indicatorNotes.to follow: the first piece comes after the second

annotation.surface: A war correspondent is appointed to cover the next conflict.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nam is the American slang name for Vietnam and its war.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: when a new captain or minister is announced, the paper says who has been put in the post.

entries.clue: One at funeral more upset around holder of ashes (7)

indicatorNotes.upset: turned over, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.around: the letters wrap around the next piece

blocks.note: MORE rearranged, split around the urn

annotation.surface: A funeral scene: one of the family grows more upset gathered round the urn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as grief at the graveside; it only shuffles 'more', and the shuffled letters wrap around the holder of ashes.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by role: the people who come to grieve the dead are the ones attending the funeral.

entries.clue: Best to drink with me during break (9)

indicatorNotes.during: inside the period of, so ME goes inside

annotation.surface: An invitation for the best part of the day: come and drink with me during the break.
annotation.walkthrough: SUP, then REST holding ME.
annotation.definitionFit: A rare superlative of supreme, highest of all, which makes a fair if clunky match for the top of the ranking.

entries.clue: Loyal group of teachers standing to receive top grade in school (7)

indicatorNotes.standing: stood up, so in a down clue the word reads upwards
indicatorNotes.receive: to receive a guest is to take them in, so A goes inside TUN
indicatorNotes.in: the result sits inside the next piece

blocks.note: the NUT, the National Union of Teachers, a British union

annotation.surface: A loyal teachers' union takes a stand, holding out for a top grade at school.
annotation.walkthrough: NUT stood upright becomes TUN, takes in A to make TAUN, and that goes into SCH.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a supporter who stands firm through thick and thin is faithful.

entries.clue: Bird with inside of bill turned up to crack nut (7)

indicatorNotes.inside of: the inside of a word is what is left once its two outer letters are stripped away
indicatorNotes.turned up: turned upside down, so in a down clue it reads upwards
indicatorNotes.to crack: breaking into the next word, so it goes inside

annotation.surface: A bird works its bill to crack a nut, the inside of the beak turned up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bill' sits beside 'Bird' as a beak, and the answer bird has a famous one; here it is just a word to hollow out, and in a down clue 'turned up' reads upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the big-billed waterbird with a throat pouch is one kind of bird.

entries.clue: State of Señorita going out having dumped Romeo (7)

indicatorNotes.going out: going out and about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: R is Romeo in the phonetic alphabet; removed

annotation.surface: A romantic drama: the señorita goes out on the town having dumped her Romeo.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Romeo' reads as the lover; it is only the letter R.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Baltic republic between Latvia and Finland is a sovereign country.

entries.clue: Handy feature to capture image (9)

blocks.note: a thumb is a feature of the hand
to nail someone is to catch them

annotation.surface: A camera's handy feature for capturing an image.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Handy feature' sounds like a useful gadget function; it is a part of the hand. A thumbnail is also a handy feature in that sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A computing sense: the small preview pictures in a photo gallery are images in miniature.

entries.clue: British scrap with local animals in this? (5)

annotation.definitionNote: a cryptic description of the answer, flagged by the question mark

blocks.note: an iota is a tiny scrap

annotation.surface: A British spat with the local wildlife.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' suggests a fight beside 'animals'; it means a tiny bit, an iota.
annotation.definitionFit: A region's biota is all its living things, so its local animals belong to it.

entries.clue: Stroke from American on Number 1 court (5)

annotation.surface: A tennis report: a stroke from an American player on Number 1 Court.
annotation.walkthrough: The tennis picture makes 'Stroke' a shot; it is the medical sense. Number 1 Court is a show court at Wimbledon, the London tennis championship.
annotation.definitionFit: An ictus is a medical stroke or seizure, and also a stressed beat in verse.

entries.clue: Weak résumé (3-4)

blocks.note: first definition: an adjective for someone tired and in poor health
second definition: a noun for a summary

annotation.walkthrough: Run-down (worn out, weak) and a rundown (a quick summary) share one spelling. 'Résumé' can suggest a CV; here it is just a summary.
annotation.definitionFit: Run-down means exhausted and weak; a rundown is a summary of the main points.

entries.clue: Conservative success curtailed against a red (7)

indicatorNotes.curtailed: cur-tailed, its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: success = HIT, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A political line: Conservative success is being cut short, with a Red on the other side.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like a left-wing opponent of the Conservatives; it is a red wine.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Tuscan wine in the straw-wrapped bottle is one red among many, hence 'a red'.

entries.clue: Time to relax in living room (9,5)

blocks.note: first definition: a pause or respite
second definition, read literally: room to live in

annotation.surface: A cosy evening: time to relax in the lounge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Living room' reads as the lounge; taken literally it is room for living, space to breathe.
annotation.definitionFit: A breathing space is a short rest, and also literally room enough to breathe in.
